title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Handler Exception Close Policy Verification
verification_method: Focused HTTP/3 loopback test, adjacent RFC 9220 regression tests, SpecTrace JSON validation, generated coverage triage, and diff hygiene.
scope: This verification covers an accepted websocket Extended CONNECT tunnel whose application handler throws after the server sends a 200 response. The server is configured with status code 1008 and reason `policy`, writes that close frame, and completes the writable side of the stream.
preconditions: The WebSocket handler dispatch boundary remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0003`.
Application-selected close frames remain trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0006`.
Default handler-exception close behavior remains trace-owned by `VER-QUIC-RFC9220-0009`.
expected_result: The focused configured close-policy and adjacent WebSocket regression tests pass, the new RFC 9220 handler-exception close-policy requirement is trace-clean, SpecTrace validation accepts the artifacts, and diff hygiene is clean.
status_summary: The HTTP/3 server handler path now has locally verified configured close status and reason policy for unexpected accepted WebSocket handler exceptions. Evidence class is local same-process loopback over the repository QUIC transport; it is not external peer interoperability, published ProtocolLab evidence, or isolated-host proof.
